html:
A Dutch priest and scholar, born in Rotterdam around 1466, who became the most famous writer in Europe in the early 1500s. He died in Basel in 1536.

He wrote in Latin and moved between England, France, Italy and the Low Countries, living on patrons and the new printing trade that Gutenberg had begun. His Praise of Folly (1511) mocked greedy monks, empty rituals and foolish theologians. In 1516 he published the first printed Greek New Testament, with his own Latin translation, so readers could check the Bible against its original.

Reformers used both books. People said that Erasmus laid the egg that Luther hatched. But Erasmus wanted to reform the church from inside and would not break with Rome. In 1524 he attacked Luther's views on free will, and Luther answered harshly.

His ideal of learning, peace and tolerance made him the hero of later humanists. The European Union student exchange programme is named after him.
